topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the topic of complement, framing its complexity and importance within the course.

topics.label: Foundations and central role of C3 in complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the overarching function, nomenclature, and core molecular mechanism of complement focused on C3.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the three distinct upstream recognition routes that converge to deposit C3 and reach the trigger threshold.

topics.label: Complement effector mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream processes through which activated complement eradicates infections.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent complement from damaging host cells.

topics.label: Clinical complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic outlines the diverse clinical presentations and disease consequences caused by deficiencies in different complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the evolutionary strategies used by pathogens to circumvent complement attack, using Staphylococcus aureus as a primary model.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session and previews the upcoming topic on the adaptive immune system.
